cards.name: Sumi-e
cards.summary: Photoshop Effect (Filter Gallery) that repaints the rasterized artwork like Japanese ink-brush painting on absorbent rice paper: a wet brush loaded with black ink, rich deep blacks and soft, bleeding stroke edges. On the photo plate the dark areas spread into solid ink and the edges bleed into brushy dark strokes. On flat vector art it has nothing to stroke and only remaps brightness: every colour without a channel at 255 (a gradient, dark greys) went solid black, Illustrator's own result.
use_for: ink-wash / East Asian brush-painting treatment on a placed photo or illustration
moody, heavily inked poster background behind clean vector type
turning a flat illustration into a dark, painterly print-style plate
festival or tea / food packaging art that wants a hand-inked feel
avoid: Greyed out in CMYK documents: the Filter Gallery effects need an RGB document (File > Document Color Mode > RGB Color) or do the look in Photoshop.

Light, delicate artwork or small type: Sumi-e pushes everything toward black, so detail and counters fill in; for a lighter ink line use Effect > Brush Strokes > Ink Outlines or Effect > Sketch > Graphic Pen.
Crisp scalable output: the result is a raster at the Document Raster Effects resolution, not vector strokes.

flat vector fills: on flat or very smooth art this filter has nothing to stroke and only remaps brightness, so at these values every colour without a channel at 255 (gradients, dark greys, a flat red) goes solid black while fills with a full channel (pure orange, pure blue) survive; that is Illustrator's own result (a dialog-applied control matched the scripted render pixel for pixel), so give it a photo or textured art

params.name: Stroke Width
params.does: size of the brush strokes; wider strokes merge detail into broad ink sweeps
params.typical: 10 (dialog value at harvest); 12-14 for a bold brush look

params.name: Stroke Pressure
params.does: how much ink each stroke lays down; higher pressure blackens more of the image
params.typical: 2 (dialog value at harvest) for a lighter ink load; 5-8 for a heavy ink look; very high values go almost solid black

params.name: Contrast
params.does: contrast of the result: separates the inked darks from the paper-light areas
params.typical: 16 (harvest); 20-28 for punchy black and white

pairs_with: Effect > Texture > Texturizer for a paper grain under the ink
Transparency panel Multiply blend so the inked raster darkens what sits below
Document Raster Effects Settings (300 ppi for print before judging stroke size)
cards.scripting: item.applyEffect('<LiveEffect name="PSAdapter_plugin_Smie"><Dict data="I dataSize 68 I PrevDres 300 B go 1"/></LiveEffect>') attaches the live effect, but Stroke Width / Stroke Pressure / Contrast live in the binary 'data' descriptor that Dict data cannot carry, so the plug-in renders with fallback settings (the harvest probe, a flat red, came out solid black: this filter's brightness remap on flat fills, not a route fault). For chosen values: select the item and app.executeMenuCommand('Live PSAdapter_plugin_Smie'), which opens the 'Sumi-e (100%)' dialog with the last-used values and needs OK; or build the look once by hand, save it as a Graphic Style and apply it with doc.graphicStyles.getByName('<style>').applyTo(item). Gallery route (2026-10-13): a plain applyEffect cannot carry the dialog settings (the Photoshop parameter block is binary 'data' that Dict data cannot send); the gallery applies the effect, saves the file, writes the dialog's parameter dictionary into it and reopens it, and that route renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog (Dark Strokes control).
cards.non_destructive: yes: a live effect in the Appearance panel (double-click to edit); Object > Expand Appearance bakes it into an embedded image
cards.cost: medium: rasterizes the object at the Document Raster Effects resolution (PrevDres 300 recorded) through the Filter Gallery; slows redraw on large artwork

review.changes: the CMYK avoid line now names the real menu item File > Document Color Mode > RGB Color (harvested path), not '> RGB'; Stroke Pressure typical: dropped the unverified claim that the harvested 2 'keeps colour' (no menu-route render exists for Sumi-e; the only render is the parameterless scripted one, solid black)

verified.note: On the photo the art is repainted with a wet black-ink brush: rich deep blacks that swallow the dark areas, soft bleeding stroke edges and a warm paper tone, the sumi-e look the card describes; the flat-vector sentence now records the brightness remap (the old black gradient) instead of a darkening guess.

cards.name: Diffuse Glow
cards.summary: Photoshop Effect (Filter Gallery) that renders the artwork as if seen through a soft diffusion filter: a grainy, transparent white glow (Photoshop takes it from the background colour; in Illustrator it comes out white) spreads out from the light areas and washes the image lighter, with film-like speckle. On flat vector art colours turn paler and hazy, edges soften into a glow and fine grain appears over the fills.
use_for: dreamy, hazy soft-glow treatment on a placed photo (wedding, beauty, nostalgia)
washed-out, sun-bleached retro poster background
soft halo and grain behind a headline group to knock it back
film-grain glow on a product shot inside an Illustrator layout
avoid: Greyed out in CMYK documents: the Filter Gallery effects need an RGB document (File > Document Color Mode > RGB Color) or do the look in Photoshop.
A coloured or neon glow: the glow is light/white only; for a coloured glow use Effect > Stylize > Outer Glow or Inner Glow.
Already light artwork on a white artboard: the white glow has little to show against; it reads best on mid-tone and dark art.

Scripted pipelines that need chosen values: applyEffect cannot send Graininess / Glow Amount / Clear Amount (the scripted apply does draw with the plug-in's fallback settings: Effect_Distort_Diffuse_Glow.png shows the probe washed paler and grainy with a softened stroke, mean diff 3.58, but those values are not yours to choose); use the menu command with its dialog, a saved Graphic Style, or the gallery route (see scripting), which renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog.

params.name: Graininess
params.does: amount of speckled grain mixed into the glow
params.typical: 6 (dialog value at harvest); 0 for a clean glow, 8-10 for a gritty film look

params.name: Glow Amount
params.does: strength of the white glow added to the image
params.typical: 10 (harvest); 14-18 for an obvious bloom

params.name: Clear Amount
params.does: how much of the image stays clear of the glow; lower values let the glow spread over more of the artwork
params.typical: 15 (harvest) keeps it subtle; 3-6 for a heavy haze

pairs_with: Effect > Blur > Gaussian Blur at a small radius for a softer bloom
Transparency panel Screen or Lighten blend on a duplicate for a stronger glow
Document Raster Effects Settings (300 ppi for print before judging the grain)

For chosen values: select the item and app.executeMenuCommand('Live PSAdapter_plugin_DfsG'), which opens the 'Diffuse Glow (100%)' dialog with the last-used values and needs OK; or build the look once by hand, save it as a Graphic Style and apply it with doc.graphicStyles.getByName('<style>').applyTo(item). Gallery route (2026-10-13): a plain applyEffect cannot carry the dialog settings (the Photoshop parameter block is binary 'data' that Dict data cannot send); the gallery applies the effect, saves the file, writes the dialog's parameter dictionary into it and reopens it, and that route renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog (Dark Strokes control).

cards.name: Glass
cards.summary: Photoshop Effect (Filter Gallery) that displaces the rasterized artwork as if it were seen through a pane of textured glass; the texture (Frosted, code TxFr, was the dialog value at harvest; the dialog also offers Blocks, Canvas and Tiny Lens) sets the pattern of the refraction. On flat vector art the edges and the PGD type get wobbly, refracted outlines and gradients pick up a mottled glassy texture while large flat fills change little.
use_for: frosted-glass or shower-glass privacy look over a placed photo
obscured, refracted background behind a headline
watery, distorted texture on lettering for a title treatment
glass-block window feel on a pattern or illustration
avoid: Greyed out in CMYK documents: the Filter Gallery effects need an RGB document (File > Document Color Mode > RGB Color) or do the look in Photoshop.

Large flat colour areas: a displacement only shows where there are edges or tonal change, so a plain fill looks untouched (the scripted harvest render, run with the plug-in's fallback settings, moved only the rectangle's stroke edge: mean diff 0.436).
Text that must stay readable: high Distortion breaks letterforms; keep it low or apply it to a background copy only.

Scripted pipelines that need chosen values: applyEffect cannot send Distortion / Smoothness / Texture Type / Scaling; use the menu command with its dialog, a saved Graphic Style, or the gallery route (see scripting), which renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog.
Note the live-effect name ends in a space ('PSAdapter_plugin_Gls '): trimming it breaks the lookup.

params.name: Distortion
params.does: how far pixels are displaced by the glass texture
params.typical: 5 (dialog value at harvest) subtle; 12-18 for strongly refracted edges

params.name: Smoothness
params.does: smoothness of the glass surface: low values give sharp, broken refraction, high values smooth wavy bends
params.typical: 3 (harvest); 1-3 crunchy, 8-12 liquid

params.name: Texture Type
params.does: the glass pattern; the dialog offers Blocks, Canvas, Frosted and Tiny Lens; only the code TxFr was harvested (the dialog value at harvest)
params.typical: TxFr (Frosted; dialog value at harvest)

params.name: Scaling
params.does: size of the glass texture in percent; larger values give bigger, more readable bumps
params.typical: 100 (harvest); 150-200 to make the pattern obvious at print resolution

params.name: Invert Texture
params.does: swaps the highs and lows of the texture so the refraction bends the other way
params.typical: false (harvest)

pairs_with: Effect > Blur > Gaussian Blur before it for a softer frosted read
Opacity mask or clipping group to keep the glass to a panel of the layout
Document Raster Effects Settings (raise to 300 ppi before judging the texture size)

summer / pool / beach poster backgrounds
wobbly, liquid edge treatment on display lettering
heat-shimmer or dream-sequence distortion on artwork

Large flat colour areas: the ripples only show on edges and tonal change (the scripted harvest render, run with the plug-in's fallback settings, broke up only the rectangle's stroke edge: mean diff 0.68).
Regular, even waves: the ripples are random; for even vector waves use Effect > Distort & Transform > Zig Zag (Smooth) or Effect > Warp > Wave.

cards.name: Color Halftone
cards.summary: Photoshop Effect that simulates an enlarged printing halftone screen: each colour channel is split into a grid of dots whose size follows the tone, with each channel's grid rotated to its own screen angle, giving overlapping coloured dot rosettes. On the photo plate at Radius 28 the whole image becomes large overlapping coloured dot rosettes whose size follows the tone, and the strip and type dissolve into dots.
use_for: pop-art / comic-book dot treatment on an illustration or placed photo
retro print, newspaper or risograph-style poster texture
enlarged halftone background pattern behind a headline
multi-colour dot art for merch and stickers (expand and trace for vector dots)
avoid: Expecting dot size in points: Radius is in pixels of the rasterization, so the same value gives much smaller dots at 300 ppi than at 72 ppi; set Document Raster Effects Settings first.
Clean single-colour vector halftone: the dots are raster; for crisp vector dots expand the appearance and use Image Trace, or build them with a blend / pattern.
Small text: dots break letterforms apart.

scripted apply with a plain applyEffect: it stores the effect but draws nothing by itself (harvest render diff 0.0); use the menu command and its dialog, a graphic style saved with the values, or the gallery route (see scripting), which renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog

params.name: Radius
params.does: maximum radius of a halftone dot in pixels at the raster-effects resolution
params.typical: 8 (dialog value at harvest) fine; 20-40 for bold pop-art dots at 300 ppi

params.name: Channel 1
params.does: screen angle in degrees for the first channel (cyan in a CMYK document, red in RGB)
params.typical: 108 (harvest)

params.name: Channel 2
params.does: screen angle for the second channel (magenta / green)
params.typical: 162 (harvest)

params.name: Channel 3
params.does: screen angle for the third channel (yellow / blue)
params.typical: 90 (harvest)

params.name: Channel 4
params.does: screen angle for the fourth channel (black in a CMYK document; not used in RGB); set all channels to the same angle for aligned dots
params.typical: 45 (harvest)

cards.name: Crystallize
cards.summary: Photoshop Effect that clumps the rasterized artwork into irregular polygon cells, each filled with one solid colour, like a crystal or faceted-mosaic pattern. On flat fills only the edges become jagged and faceted; on the photo plate at Cell Size 60 the whole image breaks into a patchwork of solid-colour polygon shards and the strip edges turn faceted.
use_for: faceted, low-poly style background from a gradient or photo
crystal / gemstone or stained-mosaic texture on illustration
abstract cell pattern behind a headline
obscuring a placed photo while keeping its colours
avoid: Small Cell Size on flat vector art: cells only show where colour changes, so the harvested dialog value 10 px at 300 ppi is barely visible (menu-route render mean diff 0.141); use a much larger cell.
Crisp vector facets: the cells are raster; for true vector low-poly shapes use Object > Image Trace or draw them.
Type that must stay readable: large cells destroy letterforms.

cards.name: Mezzotint
